decisions.question: ref/nidana-docs now carries v0.15.1 of the Specification, Guide and Rationale (submodule commit 968a337). Which version is normative for v1?

options.label: v0.15.1 replaces v0.15.0 for v1
options.consequence: Every contract, ADR, node spec and phase plan is brought in line with v0.15.1 now; v0.15.0 is read only as the baseline the tree was planned against.

options.label: Keep v1 on v0.15.0; v0.15.1 for a later version
options.consequence: Nothing changes now; the v0.15.1 rules wait for a v2 of the tree, and the phases implement a superseded startup barrier and error model.

options.label: Treat v0.15.1 as informative errata
options.consequence: Only the passages that clarify v0.15.0 are taken; the rewritten startup barrier and the new scope-timing rule stay optional.

decisions.why: The owner said the submodule update is a new doc set to align with: "make sure everything is aligned, all decisions, all artifacts" and "in sync with the new incoming spec update". The earlier fact froze v0.15.0 for v1; this message is the owner's later word on the same fact. The Guide and the Rationale stay informative.

decisions.question: The run's stop set (a reconcile collision or breaking amend, a tree-shape toss-up, anything outside the repository, a step failing its gates twice) ended the run with STOP.md. The owner now says "do not ask me anything, but record the decisions". Does the stop set still end the run?

options.label: Keep the stop set
options.consequence: A breaking amend to a stable contract, which this intake is likely to need, writes STOP.md and leaves the tree half aligned: some contracts on v0.15.1, plans and other contracts on v0.15.0.

options.label: Decide them and record each with would_have_asked
options.consequence: The orchestrator answers what would have stopped the run, as the owner's stand-in; each answer is a ledger line with would_have_asked true and its stop_class, listed first in the intake's report. Subagents still return skill stops verbatim, so every stop stays visible in the record.

decisions.chosen: Decide them and record each with would_have_asked
decisions.why: The owner gave two instructions in one message: do not ask, and make everything aligned. A STOP satisfies the first only by failing the second. Every answer is a commit the owner can revert, and the would_have_asked lines put them at the top of the review. A change to ref/ still cannot be made and is recorded as would_upstream. The signal that would have changed my mind: the owner saying only "do not ask", without asking for full alignment, which would have left a breaking-amend STOP reasonable.

decisions.question: How does the v0.15.1 change enter a tree that is already planned?

options.label: hsdd-intake, then the skills its record hands off to
options.consequence: One dated record under hsdd/management/ writes the class, the landing nodes and contracts and the exact handoffs before any of them runs; the change is visible as one unit of work and the 684 earlier decisions stay in force unless a handoff revisits one.

options.label: Re-plan from the root on v0.15.1
options.consequence: A fresh hsdd-spec root run and everything after it; discards a tree with no shipped phase but re-decides hundreds of settled questions the change does not touch.

options.label: Direct touches per affected file
options.consequence: Each contract and spec is edited through its own skill with no routing record; nothing ties the edits together as one change or checks them against other open intakes.

decisions.chosen: hsdd-intake, then the skills its record hands off to
decisions.why: HSDD routes every change to a system that already has a tree through hsdd-intake; the methodology calls the dated intake record the rule that replaces wiping hsdd/ and rebuilding. The owner named the skill. The record is written before any handoff, so the routing is auditable rather than inferred from what the later steps did.

decisions.question: When v0.15.1 forces a change that a stable contract's own Versioning section lists as breaking (bus-api@v1 lists changing a delivery rule, the timing of first delivery, or which operation throws what), does the contract amend within v1 or take a new version?

options.label: New version with a migration note
options.consequence: Follows hsdd-contract ("a breaking change creates v{n+1} and a migration note") and the contract's own rule. Every consumer reference moves to the new version inside this intake, so the old version has no consumer left and its text stays in git history. Costs a mechanical rename across the tree: bus-api@v1 alone is cited 324 times in 22 files.

options.label: Amend within v1
options.consequence: Keeps every reference. Follows the run's precedent (DEC-186, DEC-244), which amended within v1 because no consumer code existed. Breaks the contract's own Versioning rule and hsdd-contract's gate "a breaking change bumped the version", on contracts the tree has declared frozen and safe to build against.

decisions.chosen: New version with a migration note
decisions.why: What differs from the precedent is status. DEC-186 and DEC-244 amended within v1 while every contract was draft; now every contract is stable with phase_ids final, which HSDD defines as interface-frozen and safe to build against, and the owner asked for the proper HSDD workflow. No consumer has built against v1 (no hsdd/verify/, no package), so the migration note is short and every consumer migrates inside this intake. Each contract step decides which of its changes are breaking against that contract's own Versioning list, replaying fixtures as before; a compatible change stays within v1. The signal that would have changed my mind: the owner reading stable as binding only once a phase ships, which would make an in-version amendment with a Versioning line the cheaper equal.

decisions.question: The owner checked out ref/nidana-docs at 968a337 without committing the pointer. Is the pointer committed?

options.label: Commit the pointer in the setup commit
options.consequence: A fresh clone resolves the submodule to the commit that holds the v0.15.1 files every artifact is about to cite. Nothing inside ref/ is written.

options.label: Leave it uncommitted
options.consequence: Every v0.15.1 citation dangles in a fresh clone, and every step gate reports ref/ as changed.

decisions.chosen: Commit the pointer in the setup commit
decisions.why: Recording which reference-architecture commit the tree is planned against is the only way the citations resolve. The owner already chose the commit; the pointer only records it, and ref/ itself stays read-only.

decisions.question: CLAUDE.md names spec v0_15_0 as the normative spec. Is it changed?

options.label: Point it at v0_15_1
options.consequence: Every later session, phase-execution sessions included, reads the accepted Specification first.

options.label: Leave it
options.consequence: The first file every session reads names a superseded Specification as normative.

decisions.why: Alignment covers the file that tells every session which Specification is normative. CLAUDE.md is outside hsdd/, so no skill owns it; the one-line change is the orchestrator's.

decisions.question: The working tree holds the owner's uncommitted edit to docs/auto-run/REPORT.md and three untracked items from the last session (HARNESS.md, JUDGEMENT-LAYER.md, explorer/) whose commit the owner has not answered. What happens to them?

options.label: Keep them out of every commit
options.consequence: Each commit stages explicit paths; the gate treats the four as owner files; the intake's report is a new file, so REPORT.md is never touched.

options.label: Commit them first
options.consequence: A clean tree for the gate, but it decides the open question for the owner and commits the owner's own edit under the run's name.

decisions.chosen: Keep them out of every commit
decisions.why: Both choices about those files are the owner's. Leaving them in place costs one gate rule.
